quote: D. H. Lehmer, 'Sujets d'étude. No. 74', Sphinx (Brussels), Vol. 8, pp. 12-13, 1938
note: The Lychrel number problem originates from D. H. Lehmer's 1938 publication in Sphinx journal, which posed the 196 palindrome problem. This is the earliest known reference to the problem, predating the modern term 'Lychrel number' (coined by Wade Van Landingham in 2002) by 64 years. The original problem asks whether 196 is a Lychrel number (never produces a palindrome through repeated reverse-and-add operations).
